summary.text: 考 is used today for “examine,” “test,” and “investigate.” A favored account analyzes it as a phonosemantic graph: reduced 老 contributes an old/elder association, while 丂 marks sound. Historical uses for “father” and “consider/estimate” are reported, but no semantic path to the current meaning is established.

formation.text: The favored phonosemantic account treats 耂 as reduced 老, contributing an old/elder association, and 丂 as a sound marker. It says the lower 匕 of 老 is commonly omitted in 考. A competing account proposes that 丂 was used for “father” first and 老 was added as a classifier. The graph’s construction therefore remains disputed.

components.text: 耂 is described as corresponding to 老 with its lower 匕 omitted. In the favored account it contributes an old/elder association. The evidence does not establish whether this exact graphic relation is positional or chronological.
The favored account assigns 丂 a sound role. Its proposed pictorial identity varies among a branch, a cane or staff, and an axe handle; its original name is not established.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Old Chinese forms for 丂 and 考 differ, and matching later readings do not establish their ancient sound relation. The depicted object and its original name are disputed.

sound.text: Both are reported with the same Middle Chinese transcription, though their reported Old Chinese reconstructions differ.
Both are reported with this Mandarin reading; the match alone does not establish the historical sound relation.

history.text: The favored account proposes that early Western Zhou writing used 老 for both “old” and “father,” then added 丂 as a sound marker to distinguish 考; the lower 匕 of 老 was often omitted. A competing account proposes that 丂 was used for “father” first and 老 was later added as a classifier.
攷 is listed as a variant of 考. The timing of their overlap and the fuller graphic history of 攷 remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The pictorial identity and original name of 丂 remain disputed. A borrowing account that depends on the depicted object’s name and a similar-sounding word is therefore unverified.
Reported examples use 考 for “father” and “consider/estimate,” and separately as a phonetic spelling for 孝 and 巧. These examples do not establish dates or a semantic path to “examine” or “test.”

丂 and 考 share reported Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings but have distinct reported Old Chinese reconstructions; the exact Old Chinese comparison was not independently confirmed against the inspected table.

Etymological analysis: 丂 (phonetic)

The entry favors an account in which early Western Zhou inscriptions used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic marker distinguished 考, with the lower 匕 of 老 usually omitted. It also records a competing account: 丂 was an original graph, proposed to depict an axe handle, borrowed for ‘father’, then given 老 as a classifier. The entry says early bronze 丂 used for ‘father’ lends that account support, but judges the 老-based account better able to explain early Western Zhou usage. These are attributed analyses, not settled formation history.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文: ‘考，老也。从老省，丂聲’ and gives 苦浩切. Its listed Guangyun categories are 溪 initial, 上 tone, 豪/皓 rhyme, open, first division. evidence.field: 考; reported bronze and Warring States uses, lines 177–179
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze 考 for ‘father’ in 兮仲鐘 and for ‘consider/estimate’ in 中山王鼎; it also reports use for 孝 in 孟姬脂𣪕, and readings as 巧 and 孝 in named Warring States bamboo texts. Its discussion says father often refers to a deceased father but not invariably. These source-reported examples support distinct uses; they do not establish a semantic development from ‘father’ to ‘examine’ or date the earliest instance of each sense. The artifacts were not independently inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 丂; proposed graphic origin and uses, lines 108–112
evidence.text: The entry attributes to 屈萬里 an analysis of oracle-bone and bronze 丂 as a branch form and as the pictographic initial of 柯; it says 屈萬里 earlier followed 說文’s axe-handle interpretation, later revising it to branch. It reports oracle-bone use as a place name, bronze use for ‘father’ and 孝, and Warring States use read as 巧. The referent and original name/pronunciation of the depicted object remain disputed; the page does not establish an axe-handle name that independently explains the loan.

evidence.text: The dictionary presents a 老-based account: early Western Zhou bronze writing used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic marker distinguished 考, and the 考 form commonly omits the lower 匕 of 老. It also reports a competing account in which 丂 was an original graph, borrowed for ‘father’, and 老 was added as a semantic classifier; the dictionary says early bronze use of 丂 for ‘father’ gives this account some support, but considers the 老-based account a better explanation of early Western Zhou evidence. It reports bronze 考 for ‘father’ in 兮仲鐘 and for ‘consider/estimate’ in 中山王鼎, alongside separate phonetic uses for 孝 and 巧 in named bronze and Warring States texts. The entry supplies no dates for those particular examples and does not establish a semantic bridge from ‘father’ to ‘examine/test’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考

evidence.field: 丂; graph interpretation and attested uses, lines 108–112
evidence.text: The entry attributes to 屈萬里 an interpretation of oracle-bone and bronze 丂 as a branch form, proposed as an early pictographic form of 柯; it says he earlier followed 說文 in interpreting it as an axe handle. The same page describes 丂 as a cane in the 老-man depiction, and reports oracle-bone use as a place name, bronze use for ‘father’ and 孝, and Warring States use read as 巧. The referent and original name or pronunciation of the depicted object are not independently established here, so an object-name-based borrowing account remains uncertain.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
